name: Laari
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 4 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

catalog_locator: Unseth 2012 §4.4 'Structure of phonological words', §4.4.1 'Intensity and stress', pp. 103-105 (page headers 'Unseth 104', 'Unseth 105'); §4.4.2 'Moraic structure' pp. 105-106; §6.3.2 p. 185; §6.4.2 p. 186. Jacquot 1971 §1.51 p. 57.
catalog_quote: Increased intensity in Laari is most commonly manifested on the initial syllable of the word, without regard to the number of syllables in the word. Increased intensity appears in the word-initial syllable in 59% of phonological words. The next largest number of words demonstrates stress on the second syllable, and the smallest number of words shows stress on the third or further syllables. ... Intensity does not appear to be attracted to heavy syllables. ... The location of increased intensity also does not appear to be correlated with tone. ... The increased intensity observed in Laari emerges most often on the first syllable, but this is only a small majority of cases. It does not seem to relate to length or tone. There are no instances in which intensity causes a contrast; no two words are distinguished solely by their stress pattern. Therefore, it seems that stress does not exist in Laari as a significant phonological entity. [p. 185] Laari has two tones, H and L. ... The tone bearing unit is the syllable rather than the mora. There are eight syllable types in Laari and no phonological stress.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Laari is a two-tone (H/L) language; the source finds no phonological word stress. Phonetically, heightened intensity falls on the word-initial syllable in a small majority (59%) of words regardless of word length, otherwise mostly on the second syllable; it is not weight-sensitive, not tied to tone, and never contrastive. Jacquot's 1971 reference grammar likewise treats tone as the only prosodic distinctive feature and never mentions stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Intensity on the 2nd syllable is the next most frequent pattern and on the 3rd or later syllable the least; when non-initial it 'often' but not overwhelmingly sits on a H-toned syllable; no phonological motivation for the shift was found; author says the area 'should be studied further along with moraic structure' (p. 186).
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological words (nouns and verbs) from a wordlist elicited in Brazzaville in 2010 from Laari speakers who are also fluent in French; 765 tokens measured (383 two-syllable, 315 three-syllable, 59 four-syllable, 8 five-syllable). Author notes French intonation (phrase-final falling pitch) may affect the data. Jacquot 1971 §1.51 (pp. 57-58): 'des traits prosodiques.. y ont également une fonction distinctive. Ils appartiennent à la catégorie du ton' — tone only, two registers.
new_statements.identity_note: All opened sources describe the Laari/Laadi of Brazzaville and the Pool region (Republic of Congo): Unseth's 2010 data are from Brazzaville speakers; Jacquot's 'laadi' is the same Brazzaville/Pool variety (Kongo H16f). Same glottocode laar1238; no dialect distinction at issue.

tone_statements.quote: Au fil de l'élicitation, il s'est avéré d'abord que le laadi est bien une langue à "cas tonal", c'est à dire que la tonalité d'un nominal est variable en contexte et que cette variation n'a rien à voir avec une quelconque opposition défini / indéfini, comme c'est le cas dans certaines autres langues de la zone H, mais est liée à la position du mot dans l'énoncé. [...] Quatre types tonals, étiquetés A, B, C et D, ont émergé de la mise en ordre des données d'observation, soit deux de plus que pour Marie Seguin mais quatre ou cinq de moins que pour André Jacquot. Pour une classification rapide du vocabulaire, c'est à dire pour sa répartition entre ces quatre types tonals, la forme du prédicatif peut à la rigueur suffire : le type A se reconnaît à son ton haut final, le type B à son ton haut préfixal, le type C à son ton haut unique et préfinal, le type D à ses deux tons hauts, préfixal et préfinal. [...] Nous posons donc les types sous-jacents °BB (ou °B) pour A, °HH (ou °H) pour B, °BH pour C, et °HB pour D.
